issues.legal_issue: Compensation is treated as paid for deemed-lapse purposes only when it is delivered to the interested person or, where payment is prevented by a recognized contingency, offered and deposited in the appropriate court.
material_facts: An award had been made, but compensation was neither delivered to the appellants nor deposited in court.
The authority retained the compensation until the appellants applied for it and submitted title documents and a surety bond; the appellants did not complete those steps.
The authority stated that other landowners who completed those steps received their compensation.
issues.conclusion: The authority’s retention of the compensation pending an application did not amount to payment; payment required delivery to the interested person or, where a recognized contingency prevented payment, an offer followed by deposit in the appropriate court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 must be read with Section 31(1) and (2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Under Section 31, the Collector must tender compensation and, if prevented from paying by the specified contingencies, deposit it in the court to which a reference may be made. A treasury deposit or mere retention by the authority is insufficient. The Court applied Pune Municipal Corporation v. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki, which binds coordinate and lesser Benches, and relied also on IVO Agnelo Santimano Fernandes v. State of Goa and Prem Nath Kapur v. National Fertilizers Corporation of India Ltd.; it reiterated the principle in Nazir Ahmad that a prescribed procedure must be followed in the prescribed manner.

predicates.compensation_payment_assessment_in_acqui: The court is assessing whether compensation was paid in an acquisition proceeding in which deemed lapse is in issue.
predicates.compensation_delivered: The authority delivered the compensation to the person entitled to it.
predicates.compensation_offered: The authority offered the compensation to the person entitled to it.
predicates.recognized_payment_impediment: A lack of consent to receive payment, absence of a person competent to alienate the land, or a dispute over entitlement or apportionment prevented payment.
predicates.compensation_deposited_in_reference_cour: After payment was prevented, the authority deposited the compensation in the court where a reference concerning the award could be made.

issues.definition: In an acquisition-lapse proceeding, compensation counts as paid if it was delivered, or if it was offered and a recognized impediment led to its deposit in the reference court.

issues.legal_issue: An acquisition under the earlier land-acquisition regime is deemed to have lapsed when the award was made at least five years before commencement of the new regime and either possession was not taken or compensation was not paid.
material_facts: The award was made in 1968, well over five years before the new regime commenced on 1 January 2014.
The compensation was not delivered to the appellants and was not deposited in court; it remained with the authority pending an application by the appellants.
Whether possession had been taken was disputed, and the Court did not decide that question because the compensation had not been paid.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was deemed to have lapsed because the award was sufficiently old and compensation had not been paid. The Government could initiate fresh acquisition proceedings under the new regime if it chose to do so.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 applies where an award under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 predates commencement of the 2013 Act by at least five years and either possession has not been taken or compensation has not been paid. The Court applied the meaning of payment set out in Pune Municipal Corporation v. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki and the other decisions it cited, including Union of India v. Shiv Raj, Bimla Devi v. State of Haryana, Competent Automobiles Co. Ltd. v. Union of India, Radiance Fincap (P) Ltd. v. Union of India and Rajiv Chaudhari HUF v. Union of India.

rule.if: deemed_lapse_acquisition_proceeding and award_at_least_five_years_old and (possession_not_taken or compensation_not_paid)

predicates.deemed_lapse_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether an acquisition under an earlier land-acquisition regime has lapsed under a later regime.
predicates.award_at_least_five_years_old: The award was made at least five years before the later regime commenced.
predicates.possession_not_taken: The acquiring authority had not taken possession of the acquired land.
predicates.compensation_not_paid: The authority had neither delivered the compensation nor, when payment was prevented by a recognized contingency, offered it and deposited it in the appropriate court.

issues.definition: In a deemed-lapse acquisition proceeding, an acquisition is treated as lapsed when the award is at least five years old and either possession was not taken or compensation was not paid.
